facts.title: Tax your bank takes on money from abroad
facts.text: When money from a client abroad reaches your bank in Pakistan, the bank takes income tax from it under section 154A. The rate is 0.25% if you are an IT exporter registered with and certified by PSEB, and 1% for everyone else. These rates are set for tax years 2024 to 2029.

facts.title: Active Taxpayer List
facts.text: For this tax, FBR's rate card shows the same rate whether or not you are on the Active Taxpayer List.

facts.title: When the bank's tax is final
facts.text: The tax the bank takes is a final tax on that income only if you file your income tax return, file your withholding tax statements if you are required to, and file sales tax returns if you are required to. PSEB-registered IT exporters do not need the sales tax returns for this purpose. No credit is given for tax paid in another country.

facts.title: Choosing not to be taxed this way
facts.text: You can choose each year, when you file your return, not to be taxed this way. LanceraOS cannot tell you what this does to the tax your bank already took. Ask a tax advisor before you choose.

facts.title: Expenses
facts.text: When the bank's tax is the final tax, it is a percentage of the money you received. Your business expenses do not reduce it.

facts.title: Normal rates
facts.text: Income that is not taxed this way is taxed at the normal rates for non-salaried people. For tax year 2027 nothing is payable up to Rs 600,000, then the rates step up to 15%, 20%, 30% and 40%, and 45% above Rs 5,600,000. A 10% surcharge on the tax applies when taxable income is above Rs 10,000,000.

facts.title: Tax year
facts.text: A tax year runs from 1 July to 30 June and is named for the year it ends in. Tax year 2027 is 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2027.

facts.title: Return due date
facts.text: The income tax return for a tax year is due by 30 September after the year ends. FBR has often moved this date, so check FBR for the current date.
